en.title: 8 Iconic Cameos in Spider-Man: Brand New Day You Can't Miss
en.summary: From returning villains to beloved street-level heroes, 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' is packed with unforgettable cameos that deepen its comic-book mythology.
en.body:
## 1. Michael Keaton as Adrian Toomes/Vulture
Keaton's menacing return as the Vulture is more than just fan service; it’s a crucial anchor to Peter's past and the consequences of his actions. His chilling presence in a scene at the Raft, a maximum-security prison, reminds us that even out of costume, Toomes is a formidable threat.

## 2. Jon Bernthal as Frank Castle/The Punisher
Seeing Bernthal back as Frank Castle, even briefly, is a powerful jolt for fans of Netflix's Marvel shows. His gruff, no-nonsense demeanor provides a stark contrast to Spider-Man's youthful idealism, hinting at darker corners of the MCU.

## 3. Naomi Watts as E.V.
While her role as Mary Jane Watson in Sam Raimi's trilogy is legendary, Watts's surprise appearance as E.V. in 'Brand New Day' is a delightful nod to her past cinematic connections. Her brief, impactful scene adds a layer of meta-commentary for long-time fans.

## 4. Rosario Dawson as Claire Temple
Though her scene was ultimately cut from the theatrical release, Dawson's reprisal as the Night Nurse, Claire Temple, was confirmed. This inclusion would have further solidified her role as a linchpin for heroes in the MCU, offering crucial medical aid.

## 5. Tom Holland as Peter Parker/Spider-Man
It might seem obvious, but Holland’s central performance is the heart of the film. His ability to embody both the high-schooler and the seasoned hero, especially when facing multiversal chaos, is what makes the entire spectacle land.

## 6. Zendaya as Michelle Jones-Watson
Zendaya’s MJ is no longer just a love interest; she's an active participant in Peter's superhero life. Her sharp wit and unwavering support in 'Brand New Day' prove she's an essential partner, even when the stakes are impossibly high.

## 7. Mark Ruffalo as Bruce Banner/Hulk
Having Ruffalo pop up as Bruce Banner, perhaps offering some scientific insight or a gruff word of advice, connects 'Brand New Day' directly to the broader Avengers narrative. His presence grounds the fantastical elements with a touch of familiar MCU gravitas.

## 8. Stan Lee as a Multiversal Janitor (Implied)
While not a direct on-screen appearance, the spirit of Stan Lee is felt throughout the film, particularly in a brief moment where a janitor in the background bears a striking resemblance to the legendary co-creator. It’s a subtle, heartfelt tribute that honors his legacy within the Spider-Man universe.
Bottom Line: These cameos aren't just fun Easter eggs; they're vital threads weaving together the rich tapestry of Spider-Man's cinematic history and the wider MCU.

content_raw: Spoiler Alert: This list contains spoilers for Spider-Man: Brand New Day. The newest installment in the Tom Holland Spider-Man franchise, Spider-Man: Brand New Day , is finally here, and it is considered the best of the franchise. This fourth Spidey production in the Marvel Cinematic Universe isn't just a great film, but it is a gigantic treat for any fan of the Wall-Crawler's comic book mythology .
